name: Intuit
summary: Intuit makes TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma and Mailchimp, and its careers site describes final interviews built around a 'craft demonstration': you present a solution or case to members of the hiring team, then meet assessors, a team member and a manager. Intuit publishes five operating values, such as Customer Obsession and Courage, and candidates commonly report interviewers listening for them.
rounds: Online coding assessment or technical screen for many engineering roles
Interview set-up: engineers often get time to work on a technical problem before presenting it
Craft demonstration: present your solution or case to several members of the hiring team
Assessors interview that digs into your skills and your case
Team member interview on values and the environments where you do your best work
Manager interview on motivation, successes and lessons
looks_for: Clear problem solving that you can present and defend

questions.text: Tell me about a time you fell in love with a customer's problem rather than your first solution.
covers: How you learned what the customer really struggled with
The first idea you let go of, and why
What you built instead and how it helped them

questions.text: Tell me about a bold decision you made at work. How did it turn out?
covers: Why it was bold: the risk and who doubted it
How you reduced the risk and moved quickly
The result, good or bad, and what you learned

questions.text: Tell me about a time you did the right thing when it would have been easier not to.
covers: The situation and the easier option
What you did and what it cost you
Why trust mattered more, and how it turned out

questions.text: Tell me about a time a teammate's different view changed your decision.
covers: Your original view and theirs
How you listened and tested their point
The better decision and what it taught you about diverse views

questions.text: How would you present a technical solution to a panel: framing the problem, showing your work and handling questions?
covers: Starting with the problem and your approach before the details
Showing the key part of the code or design, not all of it
Naming trade-offs and what you'd do with more time, then inviting questions

questions.text: How would you design a system that imports a small business's bank transactions each day and sorts them into categories?
covers: Connecting securely to banks and handling missing or late data
Categorising with rules first, then learning from the user's corrections
Avoiding duplicate transactions and keeping a clear audit trail

questions.text: Traffic to a tax-filing product spikes sharply before a filing deadline. How would you prepare the service?
covers: Estimating the peak from past seasons and load testing early
Scaling the busy parts and protecting the critical path, such as submitting a return
Freezing risky changes before the peak and having a rollback plan

questions.text: How would you protect customers' financial data in an app, from sign-in to storage?
covers: Strong sign-in: multi-factor authentication and secure sessions
Encryption in transit and at rest, and least-privilege access
Logging, monitoring and a plan for responding to a breach

questions.text: A customer says their invoice totals don't match their own records. How would you investigate?
covers: Getting a specific example and reproducing it
Checking rounding, taxes, currency and edits made after sending
Fixing it for the customer and checking whether others are affected

questions.text: How would you test whether a new onboarding flow helps small businesses get started faster?
covers: Defining 'started': the first invoice sent or the first account connected
An A/B test with guardrails such as support contacts or drop-offs
How long to run it and what result would change the decision

questions.text: Why Intuit? Which of its products have you used, and what would you improve?
covers: A reason tied to Intuit's customers or products
A real experience with a product, or a close look at one
One improvement and who it would help

questions.text: Which of Intuit's values do you relate to most, and when have you acted on it?
covers: One value, named once
A short example from your own work
Why it matters to you

questions.text: What kind of team environment helps you do your best work?
covers: Specific conditions: feedback, ownership, pace, collaboration
An example of when you did your best work and why
How you help create that environment for others

tips: Treat the craft demonstration as a short presentation: a brief intro about you, the problem, your approach, the trade-offs and what you'd do next.
If you get set-up time before the demo, get your tools working first, then solve the core of the problem before polishing it.
Expect the assessors to follow up on your case; know why you chose each approach and what you'd change with more time.
Learn Intuit's five operating values and prepare a short story for each.
Bring questions about the team and career growth to the manager interview.
